Construction and stability of blowup solutions for a non-variational semilinear parabolic systemThanks: H. Zaag is supported by the ERC Advanced Grant no. 291214, BLOWDISOL and by the ANR project ANAÉ ref. ANR-13-BS01-0010-03.
—————–
August 24, 2026

Abstract.

We consider the following parabolic system whose nonlinearity has no gradient structure:

{∂tu=Δ​u+|v|p−1​v,∂tv=μ​Δ​v+|u|q−1​u,u⁡(⋅,0)=u0,v⁡(⋅,0)=v0,\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\partial_{t}u=\Delta u+|v|^{p-1}v,&\partial_{t}v=\mu\Delta v+|u|^{q-1}u,\\ u(\cdot,0)=u_{0},&v(\cdot,0)=v_{0},\end{array}\right.

in the whole space ℝN\mathbb{R}^{N}, where p,q>1p,q>1 and μ>0\mu>0. We show the existence of initial data such that the corresponding solution to this system blows up in finite time T⁡(u0,v0)T(u_{0},v_{0}) simultaneously in uu and vv only at one blowup point aa, according to the following asymptotic dynamics:

{u⁡(x,t)∼Γ​[(T−t)​(1+b​|x−a|2(T−t)​|log⁡(T−t)|)]−(p+1)p​q−1,v⁡(x,t)∼γ​[(T−t)​(1+b​|x−a|2(T−t)​|log⁡(T−t)|)]−(q+1)p​q−1,\left\{\begin{array}[]{c}u(x,t)\sim\Gamma\left[(T-t)\left(1+\dfrac{b|x-a|^{2}}{(T-t)|\log(T-t)|}\right)\right]^{-\frac{(p+1)}{pq-1}},\\ v(x,t)\sim\gamma\left[(T-t)\left(1+\dfrac{b|x-a|^{2}}{(T-t)|\log(T-t)|}\right)\right]^{-\frac{(q+1)}{pq-1}},\end{array}\right.

with b=b⁡(p,q,μ)>0b=b(p,q,\mu)>0 and (Γ,γ)=(Γ⁡(p,q),γ⁡(p,q))(\Gamma,\gamma)=(\Gamma(p,q),\gamma(p,q)). The construction relies on the reduction of the problem to a finite dimensional one and a topological argument based on the index theory to conclude. Two major difficulties arise in the proof: the linearized operator around the profile is not self-adjoint even in the case μ=1\mu=1; and the fact that the case μ≠1\mu\neq 1 breaks any symmetry in the problem. In the last section, through a geometrical interpretation of quantities of blowup parameters whose dimension is equal to the dimension of the finite dimensional problem, we are able to show the stability of these blowup behaviors with respect to perturbations in initial data.

Key words and phrases: 
Blowup solution, Blowup profile, Stability, Semilinear parabolic system

1. Introduction.

In this paper we are concerned with finite time blowup for the semilinear parabolic system:

{∂tu=Δ​u+|v|p−1​v,∂tv=μ​Δ​v+|u|q−1​u,u⁡(⋅,0)=u0,v⁡(⋅,0)=v0,\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\partial_{t}u=\Delta u+|v|^{p-1}v,&\partial_{t}v=\mu\Delta v+|u|^{q-1}u,\\ u(\cdot,0)=u_{0},&v(\cdot,0)=v_{0},\end{array}\right. (1.1)

in the whole space ℝN\mathbb{R}^{N}, where

p,q>1,μ>0.p,q>1,\quad\mu>0.

The local Cauchy problem for (1.1) can be solved in L∞​(ℝN)×L∞​(ℝN)L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N})\times L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N}). We denote by T=T(u0,v0)∈(0,+∞]T=T(u_{0},v_{0})\in(0,+\infty] the maximal existence time of the classical solution (u,v)(u,v) of problem (1.1). If T<+∞T<+\infty, then the solution blows up in finite time TT in the sense that

limt→T(‖u⁡(t)‖L∞​(ℝN)+‖v⁡(t)‖L∞​(ℝN))=+∞.\lim_{t\to T}(\|u(t)\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N})}+\|v(t)\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N})})=+\infty.

In that case, TT is called the blowup time of the solution. A point a∈ℝNa\in\mathbb{R}^{N} is said to be a blowup point of (u,v)(u,v) if (u,v)(u,v) is not locally bounded near (a,T)(a,T) in the sense that |u⁡(xn,tn)|+|v⁡(xn,tn)|→+∞|u(x_{n},t_{n})|+|v(x_{n},t_{n})|\to+\infty for some sequence (xn,tn)→(a,T)(x_{n},t_{n})\to(a,T) as n→+∞n\to+\infty. We say that the blowup is simultaneous if

lim supt→T‖u⁡(t)‖L∞​(ℝN)=lim supt→T‖v⁡(t)‖L∞​(ℝN)=+∞,\limsup_{t\to T}\|u(t)\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N})}=\limsup_{t\to T}\|v(t)\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N})}=+\infty, (1.2)

and that it is non-simultaneous if (1.2) does not hold, i.e. if one of the two components remains bounded on ℝN×[0,T)\mathbb{R}^{N}\times[0,T). For the system (1.1), it is easy to see that the blowup is always simultaneous. Indeed, if uu is uniformly bounded on ℝN×[0,T)\mathbb{R}^{N}\times[0,T), then the second equation would yield a uniform bound on vv. More specifically, we say that uu and vv blow up simultaneously at the same point a∈ℝNa\in\mathbb{R}^{N} if aa is a blowup point both for uu and vv.

In the case of a single equation, namely when system (1.1) is reduced to the scalar equation

∂tu=Δ​u+|u|p−1​u,u⁡(⋅,0)=u0,p>1,\partial_{t}u=\Delta u+|u|^{p-1}u,\quad u(\cdot,0)=u_{0},\quad p>1, (1.3)

the blowup question for equation (1.3) has been studied intensively by many authors and no list can be exhaustive. Let us sketch the main results for the case of the equation (1.3). Considering uu a blowup solution to (1.3) and TT its blowup time, we know from Giga and Kohn [GK87] that

∀(x,t)∈ℝN×[0,T),|u⁡(x,t)|≤C​(T−t)−1p−1,\forall(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^{N}\times[0,T),\quad|u(x,t)|\leq C(T-t)^{-\frac{1}{p-1}},

for some positive constant CC, provided that 1<p≤3​N+83​N−41<p\leq\frac{3N+8}{3N-4} or 1<p<N+2N−21<p<\frac{N+2}{N-2} with u0≥0u_{0}\geq 0. This result was extended by Giga, Matsui and Sasayama [GMS04] for all 1<p<N+2N−21<p<\frac{N+2}{N-2} without assuming the non-negativity of initial data.

The study of the blow-up behavior of solution (1.3) is done through the introduction of similarity variables:

WT,a​(y,s)=(T−t)1p−1​u​(x,t),y=x−aT−t,s=−log⁡(T−t),W_{T,a}(y,s)=(T-t)^{\frac{1}{p-1}}u(x,t),\quad y=\frac{x-a}{\sqrt{T-t}},\quad s=-\log(T-t),

where aa may or not be a blow-up point of uu. From (1.3), we see that WT,aW_{T,a} solves the new equation in (y,s)∈ℝN×[−logT,+∞)(y,s)\in\mathbb{R}^{N}\times[-\log T,+\infty):

∂sWT,a=Δ​WT,a−12​y⋅∇WT,a−WT,ap−1+|WT,a|p−1​WT,a.\partial_{s}W_{T,a}=\Delta W_{T,a}-\frac{1}{2}y\cdot\nabla W_{T,a}-\frac{W_{T,a}}{p-1}+|W_{T,a}|^{p-1}W_{T,a}. (1.4)

According to Giga and Kohn in [GK89] (see also [GK85, GK87]), we know that: If aa is a blow-up point of uu, then

limt→T(T−t)1p−1​u​(a+y​T−t,t)=lims→+∞WT,a​(y,s)=±κ,\lim_{t\to T}(T-t)^{\frac{1}{p-1}}u(a+y\sqrt{T-t},t)=\lim_{s\to+\infty}W_{T,a}(y,s)=\pm\kappa, (1.5)

uniformly on compact sets |y|≤R|y|\leq R, where κ=(p−1)−1p−1\kappa=(p-1)^{-\frac{1}{p-1}}.

This estimate has been refined until the higher order by Filippas, Kohn and Liu [FK92], [FL93], Herrero and Velázquez [HV92a], [HV93], [Vel92], [Vel93b], [Vel93a]. More precisely, they classified the behavior of WT,a​(y,s)W_{T,a}(y,s) for |y||y| bounded, and showed that one of the following cases occurs (up to replacing uu by −u-u if necessary),

∙\bullet either there exists k∈{1,⋯,N}k\in\{1,\cdots,N\},

sup|y|≤K​s|WT,a​(y,s)−κ​(1+p−14​p​s​∑i=1kyi2)−1p−1|=𝒪⁡(log⁡ss).\sup_{|y|\leq K\sqrt{s}}\left|W_{T,a}(y,s)-\kappa\left(1+\frac{p-1}{4ps}\sum_{i=1}^{k}y_{i}^{2}\right)^{-\frac{1}{p-1}}\right|=\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{\log s}{s}\right). (1.6)

∙\bullet or there exists an even integer m≥4m\geq 4 and constant cαc_{\alpha} not all zero such that

sup|y|≤K​e(12−1m)​s|WT,a​(y,s)−κ​(1+e−(1−m2)​s​∑|α|=mcα​yα)−1p−1|=o⁡(1),\sup_{|y|\leq Ke^{\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{m}\right)s}}\left|W_{T,a}(y,s)-\kappa\left(1+e^{-\left(1-\frac{m}{2}\right)s}\sum_{|\alpha|=m}c_{\alpha}y^{\alpha}\right)^{-\frac{1}{p-1}}\right|=o(1),

where the homogeneous multilinear form ∑|α|=mcα​yα\sum_{|\alpha|=m}c_{\alpha}y^{\alpha} is non-negative.

From Bricmont and Kupiainen [BK94], Herrero and Velázquez [HV93], we have examples of initial data leading to each of the above mentioned scenarios. Moreover, Herrero and Velázquez [HV92b] proved that the asymptotic behavior (1.6) is generic in the one dimensional case, and they announced the same for the higher dimensional case, but they never published it. Note also that the asymptotic profile described in (1.6) with k=Nk=N has been proved to be stable with respect to perturbations in the initial data or the nonlinearity by Merle and Zaag in [MZ97] (see also Fermanian, Merle and Zaag [FMZ00], [FZ00], Nguyen and Zaag [NZ16b] for other proofs of the stability).

As for system (1.1), much less result is known, in particular in the study of the asymptotic behavior of the solution near singularities. As far as we know, the only available results concerning the blowup behavior are due to Andreucci, Herrero and Velázquez [AHV97] and Zaag [Zaa01] where the system (1.1) is considered with μ=1\mu=1.

When μ=1\mu=1, according to Escobedo and Herrero [EH91a] (see also [EH91b]), we know that any nontrivial positive solution of (1.1) which is defined for all x∈ℝNx\in\mathbb{R}^{N} must necessarily blow up in finite time if

p​q>1,andmax⁡{p,q}+1p​q−1≥N2,pq>1,\quad\text{and}\quad\frac{\max\{p,q\}+1}{pq-1}\geq\frac{N}{2},

and both functions u⁡(x,t)u(x,t) and v⁡(x,t)v(x,t) must blow up simultaneously. See also [EH93] for the case of boundary value problems.

In [AHV97], the authors proved that if

p​q>1,andq⁡(p⁡(N−2))<N+2orp⁡(q⁡(N−2))<N+2,pq>1,\quad\text{and}\quad q(p(N-2))<N+2\quad\text{or}\quad p(q(N-2))<N+2, (1.7)

then every positive solution (u,v)(u,v) of (1.1) exhibits the Type I blowup, namely that there exists some constant C>0C>0 such that

‖u⁡(t)‖L∞​(ℝN)≤C​u¯​(t),‖v⁡(t)‖L∞​(ℝN)≤C​v¯​(t),\|u(t)\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N})}\leq C\bar{u}(t),\quad\|v(t)\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N})}\leq C\bar{v}(t), (1.8)

where (u¯,v¯)(\bar{u},\bar{v}) solves the following ODE system

u¯′=v¯p,v¯′=u¯q,u¯​(T)=v¯​(T)=+∞,\bar{u}^{\prime}=\bar{v}^{p},\quad\bar{v}^{\prime}=\bar{u}^{q},\quad\bar{u}(T)=\bar{v}(T)=+\infty,

whose solution is explicitly given by

u¯​(t)=Γ​(T−t)−p+1p​q−1,v¯​(t)=γ​(T−t)−q+1p​q−1\bar{u}(t)=\Gamma(T-t)^{-\frac{p+1}{pq-1}},\quad\bar{v}(t)=\gamma(T-t)^{-\frac{q+1}{pq-1}}

where (Γ,γ)(\Gamma,\gamma) defined by

γp=Γ⁡(p+1p​q−1),Γq=γ⁡(q+1p​q−1).\gamma^{p}=\Gamma\left(\frac{p+1}{pq-1}\right),\quad\Gamma^{q}=\gamma\left(\frac{q+1}{pq-1}\right). (1.9)

The estimate (1.8) has also been proved by Caristi and Mitidieri [CM94] in a ball under assumptions on pp and qq different from (1.7). See also Deng [Den96], Fila and Souplet [FS01] for other results relative to estimate (1.8).

The study of blowup solutions for system (1.1) is done through the introduction of the following similarity variables for all a∈ℝNa\in\mathbb{R}^{N} (aa may or may not be a blowup point):

ΦT,a(y,s)=(T−t)p+1p​q−1u(x,t),ΨT,a(y,s)=(T−t)q+1p​q−1v(x,t),wherey=x−aT−t,s=−log⁡(T−t).\begin{array}[]{c}\Phi_{T,a}(y,s)=(T-t)^{\frac{p+1}{pq-1}}u(x,t),\quad\Psi_{T,a}(y,s)=(T-t)^{\frac{q+1}{pq-1}}v(x,t),\\ \\ \text{where}\quad y=\dfrac{x-a}{\sqrt{T-t}},\quad s=-\log(T-t).\end{array} (1.10)

From (1.1), (ΦT,a,ΨT,a)(\Phi_{T,a},\Psi_{T,a}) (or (Φ,Ψ)(\Phi,\Psi) for simplicity) satisfy the following system: for all (y,s)∈ℝN×[−logT,+∞)(y,s)\in\mathbb{R}^{N}\times[-\log T,+\infty),

∂sΦ=Δ​Φ−12​y⋅∇Φ−(p+1p​q−1)​Φ+|Ψ|p−1​Ψ,∂sΨ=μ​Δ​Ψ−12​y⋅∇Ψ−(q+1p​q−1)​Ψ+|Φ|p−1​Φ.\begin{array}[]{ll}\partial_{s}\Phi&=\Delta\Phi-\dfrac{1}{2}y\cdot\nabla\Phi-\left(\dfrac{p+1}{pq-1}\right)\Phi+|\Psi|^{p-1}\Psi,\\ &\\ \partial_{s}\Psi&=\mu\Delta\Psi-\dfrac{1}{2}y\cdot\nabla\Psi-\left(\dfrac{q+1}{pq-1}\right)\Psi+|\Phi|^{p-1}\Phi.\end{array} (1.11)

Assuming (1.8) holds, namely that

∀a∈ℝN,‖ΦT,a​(s)‖L∞​(ℝN)+‖ΨT,a​(s)‖L∞​(ℝN)≤C,∀s≥−log⁡T,\forall a\in\mathbb{R}^{N},\quad\|\Phi_{T,a}(s)\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N})}+\|\Psi_{T,a}(s)\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N})}\leq C,\quad\forall s\geq-\log T,

and considering a∈ℝNa\in\mathbb{R}^{N} a blowup point of (u,v)(u,v), we know from [AHV97] that (remind that we are considering the case when μ=1\mu=1)
∙\bullet either (ΦT,a,ΨT,a)(\Phi_{T,a},\Psi_{T,a}) goes to (Γ,γ)(\Gamma,\gamma) exponentially fast,
∙\bullet or there exists k∈{1,⋯,N}k\in\{1,\cdots,N\} such that after an orthogonal change of space coordinates and up to replacing (u,v)(u,v) by (−u,−v)(-u,-v) if necessary,

ΦT,a​(y,s)=Γ−c1s​(p+1)​Γ​∑i=1k(yi2−2)+o⁡(1s),ΨT,a​(y,s)=γ−c1s​(q+1)​γ​∑i=1k(yi2−2)+o⁡(1s),\begin{array}[]{ll}\Phi_{T,a}(y,s)&=\Gamma-\dfrac{c_{1}}{s}(p+1)\Gamma\sum\limits_{i=1}^{k}(y_{i}^{2}-2)+o\left(\dfrac{1}{s}\right),\\ &\\ \Psi_{T,a}(y,s)&=\gamma-\dfrac{c_{1}}{s}(q+1)\gamma\sum\limits_{i=1}^{k}(y_{i}^{2}-2)+o\left(\dfrac{1}{s}\right),\end{array} (1.12)

where (Γ,γ)(\Gamma,\gamma) is given by (1.9) and

c1=c1​(p,q)=2​p​q+p+q8​p​q​(p+1)​(q+1),c_{1}=c_{1}(p,q)=\frac{2pq+p+q}{8pq(p+1)(q+1)}, (1.13)

and the convergence takes place in 𝒞l​o​cℓ​(ℝN)\mathcal{C}^{\ell}_{loc}(\mathbb{R}^{N}) for any ℓ≥0\ell\geq 0.
In the first case, we have other profiles, some of them are different from those occurring in the scalar case of (1.3), see Theorem 3 and 4 in [AHV97] for more details. Note that the value of c1c_{1} given in (1.13) was not precised in [AHV97], but we can justify it by explicit computations as in [AHV97].

Beside the results already cited, let us mention to the work by Zaag [Zaa01] where the author obtained a Liouville theorem for system (1.1) that improves the results of [AHV97]. Based on this theorem, he was able to derive sharp estimates of asymptotic behaviors as well as a localization property for blowup solutions of (1.1). For other aspects of system (1.1), especially concerning the blowup set, see Friedman and Giga [FG87], Mahmoudi, Souplet and Tayachi [MST15], Souplet [Sou09].

In this paper, we want to study the profile of the solution of (1.1) near blowup, and the stability of such behavior with respect to perturbations in initial data. More precisely, we prove the following result.

Theorem 1.1 (Existence of a blow-up solution for system (1.1) with the description of its profile).

Consider a∈ℝNa\in\mathbb{R}^{N}. There exists T>0T>0 such that system (1.1) has a solution (u,v)(u,v) defined on ℝN×[0,T)\mathbb{R}^{N}\times[0,T) such that:
(i)(i) uu and vv blow up in finite time TT simultaneously at one blowup point aa and only there.
(i​i)(ii) There holds that

‖(T−t)p+1p​q−1​u​(x,t)−Φ∗​(x−a(T−t)​|log⁡(T−t)|)‖L∞​(ℝN)≤C|log⁡(T−t)|,‖(T−t)q+1p​q−1​v​(x,t)−Ψ∗​(x−a(T−t)​|log⁡(T−t)|)‖L∞​(ℝN)≤C|log⁡(T−t)|,\begin{array}[]{l}\left\|(T-t)^{\frac{p+1}{pq-1}}u(x,t)-\Phi^{*}\left(\dfrac{x-a}{\sqrt{(T-t)|\log(T-t)|}}\right)\right\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N})}\leq\dfrac{C}{\sqrt{|\log(T-t)|}},\\ \\ \left\|(T-t)^{\frac{q+1}{pq-1}}v(x,t)-\Psi^{*}\left(\dfrac{x-a}{\sqrt{(T-t)|\log(T-t)|}}\right)\right\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N})}\leq\dfrac{C}{\sqrt{|\log(T-t)|}},\end{array} (1.14)

where

Φ∗​(z)=Γ​(1+b​|z|2)−p+1p​q−1andΨ∗​(z)=γ​(1+b​|z|2)−q+1p​q−1,\Phi^{*}(z)=\Gamma(1+b|z|^{2})^{-\frac{p+1}{pq-1}}\quad\text{and}\quad\Psi^{*}(z)=\gamma(1+b|z|^{2})^{-\frac{q+1}{pq-1}}, (1.15)

with (Γ,γ)(\Gamma,\gamma) given by (1.9) and

b=b⁡(p,q,μ)=(p​q−1)​(2​p​q+p+q)4​p​q​(p+1)​(q+1)​(1+μ)>0.b=b(p,q,\mu)=\frac{(pq-1)(2pq+p+q)}{4pq(p+1)(q+1)(1+\mu)}>0. (1.16)

(i​i​i)(iii)\; for all x≠ax\neq a, (u⁡(x,t),v⁡(x,t))→(u∗​(x),v∗​(x))∈𝒞2​(ℝN\{0})×𝒞2​(ℝN\{0})(u(x,t),v(x,t))\to(u^{*}(x),v^{*}(x))\in\mathcal{C}^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{N}\backslash\{0\})\times\mathcal{C}^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{N}\backslash\{0\}) with

u∗​(x)∼Γ​(b​|x−a|22​|log⁡|x−a||)−p+1p​q−1andv∗​(x)∼γ​(b​|x−a|22​|log⁡|x−a||)−q+1p​q−1,u^{*}(x)\sim\Gamma\left(\frac{b|x-a|^{2}}{2|\log|x-a||}\right)^{-\frac{p+1}{pq-1}}\quad\text{and}\quad v^{*}(x)\sim\gamma\left(\frac{b|x-a|^{2}}{2|\log|x-a||}\right)^{-\frac{q+1}{pq-1}},

as |x−a|→0|x-a|\to 0.

Remark 1.2.

The derivation of the blowup profile (1.15) can be understood through a formal analysis in Section 2 below. However, we would like to emphasize on the fact that the particular value of b=b⁡(p,q,μ)>0b=b(p,q,\mu)>0 given in (1.16) is crucially needed in various algebraic identities in the rigorous proof.

Remark 1.3.

The initial data for which system (1.1) has a solution blowing up in finite time TT at only one blowup point aa and verifying (1.14) is given by formula (4.2), which is expressed in the original variables as follows:

Remark 1.4.

We will only give the proof when N=1N=1. Indeed, the computation of the eigenfunctions (Lemma 3.2) of the linearized operator ℋ+M​c\mathscr{H}+Mc defined in (3.4) and (3.5) and the projection of (3.3) on the eigenspaces (Lemma 3.4) become much more complicated when N≥2N\geq 2. Besides, the ideas are exactly the same.

Remark 1.5.

Note that the constructed solution in Theorem 1.1 is of Type I, which means that it satisfies (1.8). Therefore, our result indicates that there exist solutions to (1.1) exhibiting the Type I blowup for all p,q>1p,q>1 and N≥1N\geq 1, even when (1.7) doesn’t hold.

The result of Theorem 1.1 holds for more general nonlinearities than (1.1), namely that the nonlinear terms in (1.1) are replaced by

As a consequence of our techniques, we show the stability of the constructed solution with respect to perturbations in initial data. More precisely, we have the following result.

Theorem 1.8 (Stability of the blowup profile (1.15)).

Let (u^0,v^0)(\hat{u}_{0},\hat{v}_{0}) be the initial data of system (1.1) such that the corresponding solution (u^,v^)(\hat{u},\hat{v}) blows up in finite time T^\hat{T} at only one blowup point a^\hat{a} and (u^​(x,t),v^​(x,t))(\hat{u}(x,t),\hat{v}(x,t)) satisfies (1.14) with T=T^T=\hat{T} and a=a^a=\hat{a}. Then, there exists a neighborhood 𝒲0\mathscr{W}_{0} of (u^0,v^0)(\hat{u}_{0},\hat{v}_{0}) in L∞​(ℝN)×L∞​(ℝN)L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N})\times L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N}) such that for any (u0,v0)∈𝒲0(u_{0},v_{0})\in\mathscr{W}_{0}, system (1.1) has a unique solution (u,v)(u,v) with initial data (u0,v0)(u_{0},v_{0}) which blows up in finite time T⁡(u0,v0)T(u_{0},v_{0}) at only one blowup point a⁡(u0,v0)a(u_{0},v_{0}). Moreover, parts (i​i)(ii) and (i​i​i)(iii) of Theorem 1.1 are satisfied, and

|T⁡(u0,v0)−T^|+|a⁡(u0,v0)−a^|→0|T(u_{0},v_{0})-\hat{T}|+|a(u_{0},v_{0})-\hat{a}|\to 0

as (u0,v0)→(u^0,v^0)(u_{0},v_{0})\to(\hat{u}_{0},\hat{v}_{0}) in L∞​(ℝN)×L∞​(ℝN)L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N})\times L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N}).

Remark 1.9.

With the stability result, we expect that the blowup profile (1.15) is generic, i.e. there exists an open, everywhere dense set 𝒰0\mathscr{U}_{0} of initial data whose corresponding solution to (1.1) either converges to the steady state (1.9) or blows up in finite time at a single point, according the asymptotic behavior (1.14). In particular, we suspect that a numerical simulation of (1.1) should lead to the profile (1.15). Up to our knowledge, the only available proof for the genericity is given by Herrero and Velázquez [HV92b] for the case of equation (1.3) in one-dimensional case. As in [HV92b], a first step towards the genericity of the profile (1.15) is to classify all possible asymptotic behaviors of the blowup solution of (1.1) which was established in [AHV97] (see also [Zaa01]) in the case when μ=1\mu=1.

Let us now give the main idea of the proof of Theorem 1.1. Our proof uses some ideas developed by Merle and Zaag [MZ97] and Bricmont and Kupiainen [BK94] for the equation (1.3). This kind of method has been proved to be successful for various situations including parabolic and hyperbolic equations. For the parabolic equations, we would like to mention the work by Masmoudi and Zaag [MZ08] (see also the earlier work by Zaag [Zaa98]) for the complex Ginzburg-Landau equation with no gradient structure,

∂tu=(1+ı​β)​Δ​u+(1+ı​δ)​|u|p−1​u−α​u,\partial_{t}u=(1+\imath\beta)\Delta u+(1+\imath\delta)|u|^{p-1}u-\alpha u, (1.18)

where u⁡(t):x∈ℝN→u⁡(x,t)∈ℂu(t):x\in\mathbb{R}^{N}\to u(x,t)\in\mathbb{C}, p>1p>1, (β,δ,α)∈ℝ3(\beta,\delta,\alpha)\in\mathbb{R}^{3} satisfying

p−δ2−β​δ​(p+1)>0.p-\delta^{2}-\beta\delta(p+1)>0.

There are also the works by Nguyen and Zaag [NZ16a] for a logarithmically perturbed equation of (1.3) (see also Ebde and Zaag [EZ11] for a weakly perturbed version of (1.3)), by Nouaili and Zaag [NZ15] for a non-variational complex-valued semilinear heat equation, or the recent work by Tayachi and Zaag [TZ16] for the nonlinear heat equation with a critical power nonlinear gradient term,

∂tu=Δ​u+|u|p−1​u+μ​|∇u|2​pp+1with​p>3,μ>0.\partial_{t}u=\Delta u+|u|^{p-1}u+\mu|\nabla u|^{\frac{2p}{p+1}}\quad\text{with}\;\;p>3,\;\mu>0.

When p→+∞p\to+\infty, this equation is reduced to

∂tu=Δ​u+eu+μ​|∇u|2,\partial_{t}u=\Delta u+e^{u}+\mu|\nabla u|^{2},

which is studied in [GNZ16]. There are also the cases for the construction of multi-solitons for the semilinear wave equation in one space dimension by Côte and Zaag [CZ13], for the wave maps by Raphaël and Rodnianski [RR12], for the Schrödinger maps by Merle, Raphaël and Rodnianski [MRR11], for the critical harmonic heat flow by Schweyer [Sch12] and for the two-dimensional Keller-Segel equation by Raphaël and Schweyer [RS14], Ghoul and Masmoudi [GM16].

One may think that the method used in [MZ97] and [BK94] should work the same for system (1.1) perhaps with some technical complications. This is not the case, since the fact that μ≠1\mu\neq 1 breaks any symmetry in the problem, and makes the diffusion operator associated to (1.1) not self-adjoint. In other words, the method we present here is not based on a simple perturbation of the equation (1.3) treated in [MZ97] and [BK94]. More precisely, our proof relies on the understanding of the dynamics of the selfsimilar version (1.11) around the profile (1.15). In the setting (1.10), constructing a solution for (1.1) satisfying (1.14) is equivalent to construct a solution for (1.11) such that

(ΛΥ)⁡(y,s)=(ΦΨ)⁡(y,s)−(Φ∗Ψ∗)⁡(ys)→(00)as​s→+∞.\binom{\Lambda}{\Upsilon}(y,s)=\binom{\Phi}{\Psi}(y,s)-\binom{\Phi^{*}}{\Psi^{*}}\left(\frac{y}{\sqrt{s}}\right)\to\binom{0}{0}\quad\text{as}\;s\to+\infty.

Satisfying such a property is guaranteed by a condition that (Λ⁡(s)Υ⁡(s))\binom{\Lambda(s)}{\Upsilon(s)} belongs to some set 𝒱A​(s)⊂L∞​(ℝN)×L∞​(ℝN)\mathscr{V}_{A}(s)\subset L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N})\times L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N}) which shrinks to 00 as s→+∞s\to+\infty (see Definition 4.1 below for an example). Since the linearization of system (1.11) around the profile (Φ∗Ψ∗)\binom{\Phi^{*}}{\Psi^{*}} gives N+1N+1 positive modes, N⁡(N+1)2\frac{N(N+1)}{2} zero modes, and an infinite dimensional negative part (see Lemma 3.2 and Remark 3.3), we can use the method of [MZ97] and [BK94] which relies on two arguments:

- The use of the bounding effect of the heat kernel (see Proposition 5.3) to reduce the problem of the control of (Λ⁡(s)Υ⁡(s))\binom{\Lambda(s)}{\Upsilon(s)} in 𝒱A​(s)\mathscr{V}_{A}(s) to the control of its positive modes. Note that the linearized operator around the profile, that is ℋ+M​c\mathscr{H}+Mc defined in (3.4) and (3.5), is not self-adjoint. This is one of the major difficulties arising in this paper.
- The control of the positive modes thanks to a topological argument based on the index theory.

In addition to the difficulties concerning the linearized operator mentioned above, we also deal with the number of parameters in the problem (p,qp,q, and μ\mu) leading to actual complications in the analysis. According to the general framework of [MZ97], some crucial modifications are needed. In particular, we have to overcome the following challenges:

  • (i)

    Finding the profile (Φ∗,Ψ∗)(\Phi^{*},\Psi^{*}) is not obvious, in particular in determining the values of bb given by (1.13), which is crucial in many algebraic identities in the rigorous analysis. See Section 2 for a formal analysis to justify such a profile. We emphasize that the formal approach actually gives us an appreciated profile to be linearized around (see (2.8) and (2.9)).

  • (ii)

    Defining the shrinking set 𝒱A\mathscr{V}_{A} (see Definition 4.1) to trap the solution. Note that our definition of 𝒱A\mathscr{V}_{A} is different from that of [MZ97]. Here, we follow the idea of [MZ08] to find out such an appreciated definition for 𝒱A\mathscr{V}_{A}. In particular, it comes from many relations in our proof, one of them is related to the dynamics of the linearized problem stated in Proposition 5.3.

  • (iii)

    A good understanding of the dynamics of the linearized operator ℋ+M​c+V\mathscr{H}+Mc+V of equation (3.3) around the appreciated profile (φ,ψ)(\varphi,\psi) given in (2.8) and (2.9) is needed, according to the definition of the shrinking set 𝒱A\mathscr{V}_{A}. Because the behavior of the potential VV defined in (3.6) inside and outside the blowup region is different, the effect of the linearized operator is therefore considered accordingly to this region. Outside the blowup region, the linear operator ℋ+M​c+V\mathscr{H}+Mc+V behaves as one with fully negative spectrum, which greatly simplifies the analysis in this region (see Section 5.2.4). Inside the blowup region, the potential VV is considered as a perturbation of the effect of ℋ+M​c\mathscr{H}+Mc, therefore, a good study of the spectral properties of ℋ+M​c\mathscr{H}+Mc is needed. Note that the linear operator ℋ+M​c\mathscr{H}+Mc is not diagonal, but it is diagonalized (see Lemma 3.2). Using this diagonalization, we then define the projection on subspaces of the spectrum of ℋ+M​c\mathscr{H}+Mc (see Lemma 3.4).

For the proof of single blowup point (part (i)(i) of Theorem 1.1), we use part (i​i)(ii) and an extended result of [GK89] that is called no blow-up under some threshold criterion for parabolic inequalities (see Proposition 4.7). The derivation of the final profile (u∗​(x),v∗​(x))(u^{*}(x),v^{*}(x)) (part (i​i​i)(iii) of Theorem 1.1) follows from part (i​i)(ii) by using the same argument as [Zaa98] and [Mer92].

The rest of the paper is organized as follows:
- In Section 2, we first explain formally how we obtain the profile (Φ∗,Ψ∗)(\Phi^{*},\Psi^{*}) and give a suggestion for an appreciated profile to be linearized around.
- In Section 3, we give a formulation of the problem in order to justify the formal argument. We also give the spectral properties of the linear operator ℋ+M​c\mathscr{H}+Mc as well as the definition of the projection on eigenspaces of ℋ+M​c\mathscr{H}+Mc.
- In Section 4, we give all the argument of the proof of Theorem 1.1 assuming technical results, which are left to the next section.
- Section 5 is central in our analysis. It is devoted to the study of the dynamics of the linearized problem. In particular, we prove Proposition 5.3 from which we reduce the problem to a finite dimensional one.
- In Section 6, we give the proof of Theorem 1.8. Since its proof is a consequence of the existence proof (part (i​i)(ii) of Theorem 1.1), thanks to a geometrical interpretation of quantities of blowup parameters whose dimension is equal to the dimension of the finite dimensional problem, we only explain the main ideas of the proof there.

2. A formal analysis.

In this section, we give a formal analysis leading to the asymptotic behaviors described in (1.14) by means of matching asymptotic. For simplicity, we shall look for (u,v)(u,v), a positive solution of (1.1) in one dimensional case. By the translation invariant in space, we assume that (u,v)(u,v) blows up in finite time T>0T>0 at the origin, and write (Φ,Ψ)(\Phi,\Psi) instead of (ΦT,a,ΨT,a)(\Phi_{T,a},\Psi_{T,a}) for short. 3. Formulation of the problem.

In this section, we give a formulation for the proof of Theorem 1.1. We will only give the proof in one dimensional case (N=1N=1) for simplicity, but the proof remains the same for higher dimensions N≥2N\geq 2. We want to prove the existence of suitable initial data (u0,v0)(u_{0},v_{0}) so that the corresponding solution (u,v)(u,v) of system (1.1) blows up in finite time TT only at one point a∈ℝa\in\mathbb{R} and verifies (1.14). From translation invariance of equation (1.1), we may assume that a=0a=0. Through the transformation (1.10), we want to find s0>0s_{0}>0 and (Φ⁡(y,s0),Ψ⁡(y,s0))(\Phi(y,s_{0}),\Psi(y,s_{0})) such that the solution (Φ,Ψ)(\Phi,\Psi) of system (1.11) with initial data (Φ⁡(y,s0),Ψ⁡(y,s0))(\Phi(y,s_{0}),\Psi(y,s_{0})) satisfies

lims→+∞‖Φ⁡(y,s)−Φ∗​(ys)‖L∞​(ℝN)=lims→+∞‖Ψ⁡(y,s)−Ψ∗​(ys)‖L∞​(ℝN)=0,\lim_{s\to+\infty}\left\|\Phi(y,s)-\Phi^{*}\left(\frac{y}{\sqrt{s}}\right)\right\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N})}=\lim_{s\to+\infty}\left\|\Psi(y,s)-\Psi^{*}\left(\frac{y}{\sqrt{s}}\right)\right\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N})}=0, (3.1)

where Φ∗\Phi^{*} and Ψ∗\Psi^{*} are given by (1.15).

According to the formal analysis in the previous section, let us introduce Λ⁡(y,s)\Lambda(y,s) and Υ⁡(y,s)\Upsilon(y,s) such that

Φ⁡(y,s)=Λ⁡(y,s)+φ⁡(y,s),Ψ⁡(y,s)=Υ⁡(y,s)+ψ⁡(y,s),\Phi(y,s)=\Lambda(y,s)+\varphi(y,s),\quad\Psi(y,s)=\Upsilon(y,s)+\psi(y,s), (3.2)

where φ\varphi and ψ\psi are given in (2.8) and (2.9).

With the introduction of (Λ,Υ)(\Lambda,\Upsilon) in (3.2), the problem is then reduced to constructing functions (Λ,Υ)(\Lambda,\Upsilon) such that

lims→+∞‖Λ⁡(s)‖L∞​(ℝN)=lims→+∞‖Υ⁡(s)‖L∞​(ℝN)=0.\lim_{s\to+\infty}\|\Lambda(s)\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N})}=\lim_{s\to+\infty}\|\Upsilon(s)\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N})}=0.

and (Λ,Υ)(\Lambda,\Upsilon) satisfies the following system:

∂s(ΛΥ)=(ℋ+M​c+V⁡(y,s))​(ΛΥ)+(F1​(Υ,y,s)F2​(Λ,y,s))+(R1​(y,s)R2​(y,s)),\partial_{s}\binom{\Lambda}{\Upsilon}=\Big(\mathscr{H}+Mc+V(y,s)\Big)\binom{\Lambda}{\Upsilon}+\binom{F_{1}(\Upsilon,y,s)}{F_{2}(\Lambda,y,s)}+\binom{R_{1}(y,s)}{R_{2}(y,s)}, (3.3)

where

ℋ=(ℒ100ℒμ)where ℒη=ηΔ−12y⋅∇,η={1,μ},\mathscr{H}=\begin{pmatrix}\mathscr{L}_{1}&0\\ 0&\mathscr{L}_{\mu}\end{pmatrix}\quad\text{where }\;\;\mathscr{L}_{\eta}=\eta\Delta-\frac{1}{2}y\cdot\nabla,\quad\eta=\{1,\mu\}, (3.4)
M​c=(−p+1p​q−1p​γp−1q​Γq−1−q+1p​q−1),Mc=\begin{pmatrix}-\frac{p+1}{pq-1}&\;p\gamma^{p-1}\\ q\Gamma^{q-1}&\;-\frac{q+1}{pq-1}\end{pmatrix}, (3.5)
V⁡(y,s)=(0p⁡(ψp−1−γp−1)q⁡(φq−1−Γq−1)0)≡(0V1V20),V(y,s)=\begin{pmatrix}0&p\big(\psi^{p-1}-\gamma^{p-1}\big)\\ q\big(\varphi^{q-1}-\Gamma^{q-1}\big)&0\end{pmatrix}\equiv\begin{pmatrix}0&V_{1}\\ V_{2}&0\end{pmatrix}, (3.6)
(F1​(Υ,y,s)F2​(Λ,y,s))=(|Υ+ψ|p−1​(Υ+ψ)−ψp−p​ψp−1​Υ|Λ+φ|q−1​(Λ+φ)−φq−q​φq−1​Λ),\binom{F_{1}(\Upsilon,y,s)}{F_{2}(\Lambda,y,s)}=\binom{|\Upsilon+\psi|^{p-1}(\Upsilon+\psi)-\psi^{p}-p\psi^{p-1}\Upsilon}{|\Lambda+\varphi|^{q-1}(\Lambda+\varphi)-\varphi^{q}-q\varphi^{q-1}\Lambda}, (3.7)

and

(R1​(y,s)R2​(y,s))=(−∂sφ+Δφ−12y⋅∇φ−(p+1p​q−1)φ+ψp−∂sψ+μΔψ−12y⋅∇ψ−(q+1p​q−1)ψ+φq).\binom{R_{1}(y,s)}{R_{2}(y,s)}=\binom{-\partial_{s}\varphi+\Delta\varphi-\frac{1}{2}y\cdot\nabla\varphi-\left(\frac{p+1}{pq-1}\right)\varphi+\psi^{p}}{-\partial_{s}\psi+\mu\Delta\psi-\frac{1}{2}y\cdot\nabla\psi-\left(\frac{q+1}{pq-1}\right)\psi+\varphi^{q}}. (3.8)

Note that the term (F1F2)\binom{F_{1}}{F_{2}} is built to be quadratic in the inner region |y|≤2​K​s|y|\leq 2K\sqrt{s}. Indeed, we have for all K>1K>1 and s≥1s\geq 1,

sup|y|≤2​K​s|F1​(Υ,y,s)|≤C⁡(K)​|Υ|2,sup|y|≤2​K​s|F2​(Λ,y,s)|≤C⁡(K)​|Λ|2.\sup_{|y|\leq 2K\sqrt{s}}\left|F_{1}(\Upsilon,y,s)\right|\leq C(K)|\Upsilon|^{2},\quad\sup_{|y|\leq 2K\sqrt{s}}\left|F_{2}(\Lambda,y,s)\right|\leq C(K)|\Lambda|^{2}.

Therefore, since we would like to make (Λ,Υ)(\Lambda,\Upsilon) go to zero as s→+∞s\to+\infty in L∞​(ℝN)×L∞​(ℝN)L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N})\times L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N}), the dynamics of (3.3) are influenced by the asymptotic limit of its linear term,

(ℋ+M​c+V⁡(y,s))​(ΛΥ)ass→+∞.\Big(\mathscr{H}+Mc+V(y,s)\Big)\binom{\Lambda}{\Upsilon}\quad\text{as}\quad s\to+\infty.

From the definition (3.6), we see that the potential V⁡(y,s)V(y,s) has two fundamental properties that will influence strongly our analysis:

(i)(i)\; We have (V1​(⋅,s),V2​(⋅,s))→(0,0)(V_{1}(\cdot,s),V_{2}(\cdot,s))\to(0,0) in Lρ12​(ℝN)×Lρμ2​(ℝN)L^{2}_{\rho_{1}}(\mathbb{R}^{N})\times L^{2}_{\rho_{\mu}}(\mathbb{R}^{N}) as s→+∞s\to+\infty, where Lρη2​(ℝN)L^{2}_{\rho_{\eta}}(\mathbb{R}^{N}) is the weighted L2L^{2} space associated with the weight ρη\rho_{\eta} defined by

ρη​(y)=1(4​π​η)N/2​e−|y|24​η.\rho_{\eta}(y)=\frac{1}{(4\pi\eta)^{N/2}}e^{-\frac{|y|^{2}}{4\eta}}. (3.10)

In particular, the effect on VV inside the blowup region or in the inner region |y|≤K​s|y|\leq K\sqrt{s} will be a perturbation of the effect of ℋ+M​c\mathscr{H}+Mc.

(i​i)(ii)\; Outside the blowup region or in the outer region |y|≥K​s|y|\geq K\sqrt{s}, we have the following property: for all ϵ>0\epsilon>0, there exist Kϵ>0K_{\epsilon}>0 and sϵ>0s_{\epsilon}>0 such that

sups≥sϵ,|y|≥Kϵ​s|V1​(y,s)−(−p​γp−1)|+|V2​(y,s)−(−q​Γq−1)|≤ϵ.\sup_{s\geq s_{\epsilon},|y|\geq K_{\epsilon}\sqrt{s}}\left|V_{1}(y,s)-(-p\gamma^{p-1})\right|+\left|V_{2}(y,s)-(-q\Gamma^{q-1})\right|\leq\epsilon.

In other words, outside the blowup region, the linear operator ℋ+M​c+V\mathscr{H}+Mc+V behaves as

ℋ+(−p+1p​q−1±ϵ1±ϵ2−q+1p​q−1).\mathscr{H}+\left(\begin{array}[]{cc}-\frac{p+1}{pq-1}&\pm\epsilon_{1}\\ \pm\epsilon_{2}&-\frac{q+1}{pq-1}\end{array}\right).

Since the behavior of the potential VV inside and outside the blowup region is different, we will consider the dynamics for |y|≥K​s|y|\geq K\sqrt{s} and |y|≤2​K​s|y|\leq 2K\sqrt{s} separately for some KK to be fixed large.

Let us consider a non-increasing cut-off function χ0∈𝒞0∞([0,+∞))\chi_{0}\in\mathcal{C}^{\infty}_{0}([0,+\infty)), with supp​(χ0)⊂[0,2]\text{supp}(\chi_{0})\subset[0,2] and χ0≡1\chi_{0}\equiv 1 on [0,1][0,1], and introduce

where KK is chosen large enough so that various technical estimates hold. We define

(ΛeΥe)\binom{\Lambda_{e}}{\Upsilon_{e}} is the part of (ΛΥ)\binom{\Lambda}{\Upsilon} for |y|≥K​s|y|\geq K\sqrt{s}. As announced a few lines above and as we will see in Section 5.2.4, the spectrum of the linear operator of the equation satisfied by (ΛeΥe)\binom{\Lambda_{e}}{\Upsilon_{e}} is negative, which makes the control of ‖Λe​(s)‖L∞​(ℝ)\|\Lambda_{e}(s)\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R})} and ‖Υe​(s)‖L∞​(ℝ)\|\Upsilon_{e}(s)\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R})} easily.

While the control of the outer part is easy, it is not the case for the part of (ΛΥ)\binom{\Lambda}{\Upsilon} for |y|≤2​K​s|y|\leq 2K\sqrt{s}. for all (x,t)∈B(x0,r)×[T−r2,T)(x,t)\in B(x_{0},r)\times[T-r^{2},T) for some x0∈ℝx_{0}\in\mathbb{R} and r>0r>0, then (u,v)(u,v) does not blow up at (x0,T)(x_{0},T).

Although Giga and Kohn give in [GK89] the proof only for the scalar case (1.3) (see Theorem 2.1, page 850 in [GK89]), their argument remains valid for system (1.1) because of the following scaling invariant property of system (1.1): If (u,v)(u,v) solves (1.1), then

∀λ>0,(uλ​(x,t),vλ​(x,t)):=(λ2​(p+1)p​q−1​u​(λ​x,λ2​t),λ2​(q+1)p​q−1​v​(λ​x,λ2​t)),\forall\lambda>0,\quad(u_{\lambda}(x,t),v_{\lambda}(x,t)):=\left(\lambda^{\frac{2(p+1)}{pq-1}}u(\lambda x,\lambda^{2}t),\lambda^{\frac{2(q+1)}{pq-1}}v(\lambda x,\lambda^{2}t)\right),

does the same; and because the semigroup and the fundamental solution generated by η​Δ\eta\Delta with η∈{1,μ}\eta\in\{1,\mu\} have the same regularizing effect independently from η\eta. ∎

Indeed, we see from (1.14) that

and

as t→Tt\to T, hence, x0x_{0} is not a blowup point of (u,v)(u,v) from Proposition 4.7. This concludes the proof of part (i)(i) of Theorem 1.1.

We now give the proof of part (i​i​i)(iii) of Thereom 1.1. Using the technique of Merle [Mer92], we derive the existence of a blowup profile (u∗,v∗)∈𝒞2​(ℝ∗)×𝒞2​(ℝ∗)(u^{*},v^{*})\in\mathcal{C}^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{*})\times\mathcal{C}^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{*}) such that

- Part 2: We deal with system (3.3) to write ODEs satisfied by θn\theta_{n} and θ~n\tilde{\theta}_{n} for n≤Mn\leq M. 6. Stability of the constructed solution.

In this section we give the proof of Theorem 1.8. The proof strongly relies on the same ideas used in the proof of Theorem 1.1. That is the use of finite-dimensional parameters, the reduction to a finite-dimensional problem and the continuity. As the proof of Theorem 1.1, we only give the proof of Theorem 1.8 in the one dimensional case for simplicity, however, the same proof holds for higher dimensions. We claim the following which directly follows Theorem 1.8:

Proposition 6.1.

Let (u^0,v^0)(\hat{u}_{0},\hat{v}_{0}) be the initial data of system (1.1) such that the corresponding solution (u^,v^)(\hat{u},\hat{v}) blows up in finite time T^\hat{T} at only one blowup point a^\hat{a} and (u^​(x,t),v^​(x,t))(\hat{u}(x,t),\hat{v}(x,t)) satisfies (1.14) with T=T^T=\hat{T} and a=a^a=\hat{a}. Then, there exist B0≥1B_{0}\geq 1, s0≥1s_{0}\geq 1, a neighborhood ℰs0\mathcal{E}_{s_{0}} of (T^,a^)(\hat{T},\hat{a}) in ℝ2\mathbb{R}^{2} and a neighborhood 𝒲0\mathscr{W}_{0} of (u^0,v^0)(\hat{u}_{0},\hat{v}_{0}) in L∞​(ℝ)×L∞​(ℝ)L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R})\times L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}) such that the following holds: for any (u0,v0)∈𝒲0(u_{0},v_{0})\in\mathscr{W}_{0}, there exists (T,a)∈ℰs0(T,a)\in\mathcal{E}_{s_{0}} such that for all s≥s0s\geq s_{0}, (ΛT,a​(s)ΥT,a​(s))∈𝒱B0​(s)\binom{\Lambda_{T,a}(s)}{\Upsilon_{T,a}(s)}\in\mathscr{V}_{B_{0}}(s), where

where (ΦT,a,ΨT,a)(\Phi_{T,a},\Psi_{T,a}) is defined as in (1.10) with (u,v)(u,v) is the unique solution of (1.1) with initial data (u0,v0)(u_{0},v_{0}), and φ\varphi, ψ\psi are defined in (2.8) and (2.9).

Indeed, once Proposition 6.1 is proved, we deduce from part (i​i)(ii) of Proposition 5.1 and (1.10) that (1.14) holds for (u,v)(u,v). Then, Proposition 4.7 applied to (u,v)(u,v) shows that (u,v)(u,v) blows up at time TT at one single point aa. Since part (i​i​i)(iii) of Theorem 1.1 follows from part (i​i)(ii), we conclude the proof of Theorem 1.8 assuming that Proposition 6.1 holds.

Let us now give the proof of Proposition 6.1. The proof is anagolous to the case of equation (1.3) treated in [MZ97] (see also [TZ16]). For the reader’s convenience, we give here the main idea of the proof. The interested reader is kindly referred to the stability section in [MZ97] and [TZ16] for more details.

With the result of Proposition 6.2 in hands, we are ready to complete the proof of Proposition 6.1. Recall that in the existence proof given in Section 4, we had to specific choice of the two parameters (d0,d1)∈ℝ2(d_{0},d_{1})\in\mathbb{R}^{2} appearing in (4.2) in order to guarantee that (Λ⁡(s)Υ⁡(s))d0,d1∈𝒱A​(s)\binom{\Lambda(s)}{\Upsilon(s)}_{d_{0},d_{1}}\in\mathscr{V}_{A}(s) for all s≥s0s\geq s_{0} for some A≥1A\geq 1 and s0​(A)≥1s_{0}(A)\geq 1 large enough. In particular, we choose (d0,d1)∈𝒟s0(d_{0},d_{1})\in\mathcal{D}_{s_{0}} so that the initial data at s=s0s=s_{0} of (3.3) is small in 𝒱A​(s0)\mathscr{V}_{A}(s_{0}). Together with the dynamics of system (3.3) given in Proposition 5.3, we show that it stays small in 𝒱A​(s)\mathscr{V}_{A}(s) up to s=s0+λs=s_{0}+\lambda for some λ=log⁡A\lambda=\log A (see Subsection 5.2.1). In the case s≥s0+λs\geq s_{0}+\lambda, we didn’t use the data at s=s0s=s_{0}, we only used Proposition 5.3 to derive the smallness of the solution. In particular, we derive the so-called reduction of the problem to a finite-dimensional one (see Proposition 4.5). Then the topological argument for the finite-dimensional problem involving two parameters (d0,d1)(d_{0},d_{1}) allows us to conclude the existence of (d0,d1)∈𝒟s0(d_{0},d_{1})\in\mathcal{D}_{s_{0}} such that the solution of (3.3) with initial data (4.2) is trapped in 𝒱A​(s)\mathscr{V}_{A}(s) for all s≥s0s\geq s_{0}. Now, starting from (Λ¯0Υ¯0)⁡(T,a,u0,v0,σ0)\binom{\bar{\Lambda}_{0}}{\bar{\Upsilon}_{0}}(T,a,u_{0},v_{0},\sigma_{0}) at time s=s0s=s_{0} and applying the same procedure as for the existence proof including the reduction to a finite dimensional problem (see Proposition 4.5) and the topological argument involving the two parameters (T,a)(T,a), we end-up with the existence of (T¯​(u0,v0),a¯​(u0,v0))∈𝒟¯B,σ0,u0,v0(\bar{T}(u_{0},v_{0}),\bar{a}(u_{0},v_{0}))\in\bar{\mathcal{D}}_{B,\sigma_{0},u_{0},v_{0}} such that system (3.3) with initial data at time s=s0s=s_{0}, (Λ¯0Υ¯0)⁡(T¯​(u0,v0),a¯​(u0,v0),u0,v0,σ0)\binom{\bar{\Lambda}_{0}}{\bar{\Upsilon}_{0}}(\bar{T}(u_{0},v_{0}),\bar{a}(u_{0},v_{0}),u_{0},v_{0},\sigma_{0}), has a solution (Λ¯Υ¯)σ0,u0,v0\binom{\bar{\Lambda}}{\bar{\Upsilon}}_{\sigma_{0},u_{0},v_{0}} such that

(Λ¯​(s)Υ¯​(s))u0,v0,σ0∈𝒱B​(s)for all​s≥s0.\binom{\bar{\Lambda}(s)}{\bar{\Upsilon}(s)}_{u_{0},v_{0},\sigma_{0}}\in\mathscr{V}_{B}(s)\quad\text{for all}\;s\geq s_{0}.

By definition, (Λ¯0Υ¯0)⁡(T¯​(u0,v0),a¯​(u0,v0),u0,v0,σ0)\binom{\bar{\Lambda}_{0}}{\bar{\Upsilon}_{0}}(\bar{T}(u_{0},v_{0}),\bar{a}(u_{0},v_{0}),u_{0},v_{0},\sigma_{0}) is the initial data also at time s=s0s=s_{0} defined in (6.4) and (6.5), of (Λ¯Υ¯)u0,v0,σ0\binom{\bar{\Lambda}}{\bar{\Upsilon}}_{u_{0},v_{0},\sigma_{0}}, another solution of the same equation (3.3). From the uniqueness of the Cauchy problem, both solutions are equal and have the same domain of the definition and the same trapping property in 𝒱B​(s)\mathscr{V}_{B}(s). Reminding that (ΛΥ)T¯​(u0,v0),a¯​(u0,v0),u0,v0,σ0​(y,s)\binom{\Lambda}{\Upsilon}_{\bar{T}(u_{0},v_{0}),\bar{a}(u_{0},v_{0}),u_{0},v_{0},\sigma_{0}}(y,s) is defined for all (y,s)∈ℝ×[−log⁡T¯​(u0,v0),−log⁡((T¯​(u0,v0)−T⁡(u0,v0))+)](y,s)\in\mathbb{R}\times\big[-\log\bar{T}(u_{0},v_{0}),-\log((\bar{T}(u_{0},v_{0})-T(u_{0},v_{0}))_{+})\big], which implies that

T¯​(u0,v0)=T⁡(u0,v0)\bar{T}(u_{0},v_{0})=T(u_{0},v_{0})

and

(Λ⁡(s)Υ⁡(s))T¯​(u0,v0),a¯​(u0,v0),u0,v0,σ0=(Λ¯​(s)Υ¯​(s))u0,v0,σ0∈𝒱B​(s)for all​s≥s0.\binom{\Lambda(s)}{\Upsilon(s)}_{\bar{T}(u_{0},v_{0}),\bar{a}(u_{0},v_{0}),u_{0},v_{0},\sigma_{0}}=\binom{\bar{\Lambda}(s)}{\bar{\Upsilon}(s)}_{u_{0},v_{0},\sigma_{0}}\in\mathscr{V}_{B}(s)\quad\text{for all}\;s\geq s_{0}.

This concludes the proof of Proposition 6.1 as well as Theorem 1.8.

Appendix A Some elementary lemmas.

The following lemma is the integral version of Gronwall’s inequality:

Lemma A.1 (A Gronwall’s inequality).

If λ⁡(s)\lambda(s), α⁡(s)\alpha(s) and β⁡(s)\beta(s) are continuous defined on [s0,s1][s_{0},s_{1}] such that

λ⁡(s)≤λ⁡(s0)+∫s0sα⁡(τ)​λ​(τ)​𝑑τ+∫s0sβ⁡(τ)​𝑑τ,s0≤s≤s1,\lambda(s)\leq\lambda(s_{0})+\int_{s_{0}}^{s}\alpha(\tau)\lambda(\tau)d\tau+\int_{s_{0}}^{s}\beta(\tau)d\tau,\quad s_{0}\leq s\leq s_{1},

then

λ(s)≤exp(∫s0sα(τ)dτ)[λ(s0)+∫s0sβ(τ)exp(−∫s0τα(τ′)dτ′)dτ].\lambda(s)\leq\exp\left(\int_{s_{0}}^{s}\alpha(\tau)d\tau\right)\left[\lambda(s_{0})+\int_{s_{0}}^{s}\beta(\tau)\exp\left(-\int_{s_{0}}^{\tau}\alpha(\tau^{\prime})d\tau^{\prime}\right)d\tau\right].
Proof.

See Lemma 2.3 in [GK89].

∎

In the following lemma, we recall some linear regularity estimates of the linear operator ℒη\mathscr{L}_{\eta} defined in (3.4):

Lemma A.2 (Properties of the semigroup eτ​ℒηe^{\tau\mathscr{L}_{\eta}}).

The kernel eτ​ℒη​(y,x)e^{\tau\mathscr{L}_{\eta}}(y,x) of the semigroup eτ​ℒηe^{\tau\mathscr{L}_{\eta}} is given by

eτ​ℒη​(y,x)=1[4​π​(1−e−τ)]N/2​exp⁡(−|ye−τ/2−x|24​η​(1−eτ)),∀τ>0,e^{\tau\mathscr{L}_{\eta}}(y,x)=\frac{1}{\big[4\pi(1-e^{-\tau})\big]^{N/2}}\exp\left(-\frac{|ye^{-\tau/2}-x|^{2}}{4\eta(1-e^{\tau})}\right),\quad\forall\tau>0, (A.1)

and eτ​ℒηe^{\tau\mathscr{L}_{\eta}} is defined by

eτ​ℒη​g​(y)=∫ℝNeτ​ℒη​(y,x)​g​(x)​𝑑x.e^{\tau\mathscr{L}_{\eta}}g(y)=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{N}}e^{\tau\mathscr{L}_{\eta}}(y,x)g(x)dx. (A.2)

We also have the following:

(i)(i)\; ‖eτ​ℒη​g‖L∞​(ℝN)≤‖g‖L∞​(ℝN)\left\|e^{\tau\mathscr{L}_{\eta}}g\right\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N})}\leq\|g\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N})} for all g∈L∞​(ℝN)g\in L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N}),

(i​i)(ii)\; ‖eτ​ℒη​div​(g)‖L∞​(ℝN)≤C1−e−τ​‖g‖L∞​(ℝN)\left\|e^{\tau\mathscr{L}_{\eta}}\,\text{div}(g)\right\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N})}\leq\frac{C}{\sqrt{1-e^{-\tau}}}\|g\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N})} for all g∈L∞​(ℝN)g\in L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N}),

(i​i​i)(iii)\; If |g⁡(x)|≤(1+|x|M+1)|g(x)|\leq(1+|x|^{M+1}) for all x∈ℝNx\in\mathbb{R}^{N}, then

|eτ​ℒη​Π−,M​(g⁡(y))|≤C​e−(M+1)​τ2​(1+|y|M+1),∀y∈ℝN.\left|e^{\tau\mathscr{L}_{\eta}}\Pi_{-,M}(g(y))\right|\leq Ce^{-\frac{(M+1)\tau}{2}}(1+|y|^{M+1}),\quad\forall y\in\mathbb{R}^{N}.

(i​v)(iv)\; For all k≥0k\geq 0, we have

‖Π−,M​(g)1+|y|M+k‖L∞​(ℝN)≤C​‖g1+|y|M+k‖L∞​(ℝN).\left\|\frac{\Pi_{-,M}(g)}{1+|y|^{M+k}}\right\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N})}\leq C\left\|\frac{g}{1+|y|^{M+k}}\right\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{N})}.
Proof.

The expressions of eτ​ℒη​(y,x)e^{\tau\mathscr{L}_{\eta}}(y,x) and eτ​ℒηe^{\tau\mathscr{L}_{\eta}} are given in [BK94], page 554. The proof of (i)−(i​i)(i)-(ii) follow by straightforward calculations using (A.1) and (A.2). For (i​i​i)−(i​v)(iii)-(iv), see Lemmas A.2 and A.3 in [MZ08]. ∎
